facts.claim: NWS interface control document definitions (Hail Index, RPG Build 18.0)
facts.value: Section 19.1: 'This product shall provide, for each storm cell identified by the Storm Cell Identification and Tracking algorithm, the Probability of Hail, the Probability of Severe Hail, and the Maximum Expected Hail Size. The Maximum Expected Hail Size is calculated to the nearest 0.25 inch.' Section 19.2.2 lists '(b) Probability of Severe Hail in percentage', '(c) Probability of Hail in percentage', '(d) Maximum Expected Hail Size in inches'. facts.claim: PROB -999 in nx3hail_all

The ICD and the SWDI documentation do not define -999 (a text search of the ICD found only unrelated fields). Nationwide 2025-06-15: PROB -999 has 11,071 of 21,016 rows. Meaning not verified.

facts.claim: Benchland comparison: what the one-day check can and cannot say
facts.value: Window B is the usable pair: its first half (2025-06-14 12Z to 24Z) has 3,928 nationwide nx3hail rows and its second half (2025-06-15 00Z to 12Z) has 1,764, so the window is populated. Its SWDI and MRMS maxima sit about 1.5 km apart. If the MRMS units are millimetres, the MRMS maximum is 3.07 in; the unit is not verified (W1). A radar hail signature and an estimated 24-hour maximum are different quantities, and one event is not a validation; no hit or false-alarm rate is computed here.

facts.claim: ICD display rules and the UNKNOWN label
facts.value: ICD 19.2.2.1: '0.00' when both probabilities are 0%; '<0.50' when a probability is above 0% and the size is under 0.50 in; '>4.00' above 4 in; 'UNKNOWN' when characteristics cannot be determined (e.g. beyond 124 nmi). No size threshold for 'severe' (SEVPROB) is stated in the ICD or the SWDI documentation.

terms.license: No separate reuse licence was found on the SWDI pages read. NCEI open data policy NCEI-PD-10-2-02 (December 14, 2022), section 4a: 'These data are in the public domain in the United States.' The policy glossary defines an open license as: 'Open license: a legal guarantee that a data asset is made available at no cost to the public; and with no restrictions on copying, publishing, distributing, transmitting, citing, or adapting such asset.' The glossary defines the term; it does not state that SWDI carries that licence.
terms.attribution_required: Not found on the SWDI pages read.

quotes.text: These data are in the public domain in the United States. To serve our international partners and customers, NCEI will work to ensure a Creative Commons CC0 license is applied.

Open license: a legal guarantee that a data asset is made available at no cost to the public; and with no restrictions on copying, publishing, distributing, transmitting, citing, or adapting such asset.
SWDI provides a uniform way to access data from a variety of sources, but it does not provide any additional quality control beyond the processing that takes place during data archival.
The absence of SWDI data for a particular location and time doesn't mean that no severe weather occurred within those parameters.
Much of the automatically derived data in SWDI is from radar data that represents probable conditions for an event rather than a confirmed occurrence.
NCEI is currently moving its data and applications to the cloud.
Current Impact: Intermittent degraded order fulfillment services.
At this time, only NOAA personnel may access the Vaisala NLDN lightning strike data, accessing the data through the NOAA VPN only

terms.endorsement: The NOAA disclaimer sentence above is limited to external links. No statement about endorsement of derived products was found on the SWDI pages.
terms.procurement_open: Redistribution, display and commercial use of derived SWDI counts or maps, and any use of the 'experimental' bulk files, need a legal review (W10). Not decided here.

limits: The documented one-year date range is not what the service enforces for row output and grouped counts: both return HTTP 500 above 744 hours (verbatim error). Montana rows were downloaded in calendar months. A plain count accepted a two-year range.

The default nx3hail dataset is filtered to PROB 100 and MAXSIZE above 0. Only about 9.6 to 12.7 percent of Montana signatures (distinct rows, by year) are in it (see the share fact). Use nx3hail_all for the full set.

Counts are radar detections (one row per cell per radar volume, CELL_ID unique to a radar site), not hail events, storms, or damage. Distinct-row counts remove exact duplicate rows; raw rows are also given.
Exact duplicate rows are in the archive (see the duplicates fact). They are removed in the distinct counts, but NCEI has not been asked whether they are intended.

Archive gaps exist: no records for 2025-06-15 12:00 to 24:00 UTC nationwide, none for 2025-01-12 to 2025-01-19 (no inventory rows), and none for 2026-10-13. Absence of records here is not evidence of no hail. The inventory reports 24 coverage hours for 2025-06-15, so it does not reveal that gap; for 2026-10-13 the inventory has no row.

The Montana outline is the repo basemap 'land' polygon named Montana (212 vertices, one ring). It is Census-derived and simplified (tools/build_basemap.py). Points within about 1 km of the border may be misclassified. A Census 500k ring (2,633 vertices) moves the totals by 2 to 11 rows.

Positional accuracy per the SWDI documentation: about 1 km near the radar to about 4 km at 230 km. The four Montana radars are 123 to 310 km from the Benchland point, so cell positions are coarse. Mountainous areas can cause beam blockage at lower elevations.
MAXSIZE is 'MAX SIZE [IN]' per the SWDI documentation and 'Maximum Expected Hail Size in inches' per the ICD. The ICD revision used is RPG Build 18.0 (2018); newer builds were not checked.

The Benchland comparison uses one event in two 24-hour windows and one 15 km radius. Window A is incomplete in SWDI (no records for its first 12 hours). MRMS units are unknown in the GRIB header; millimetres are an assumption. No skill score is computed.

The bulk monthly files are labelled experimental. The February 2026 bulk file has records for 10 of 28 days; 16 of the 26 days with API records are missing and 10 Feb is partial (a snapshot taken before late processing). The October 2026 file matches the API.

Transient proxy resets (TLS SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL, rc 35): one first attempt for the 2025-06-15 first-five request (recovered by retry); two Montana months failed twice each (2020-11 nx3hail, 2026-02 nx3hail_all) and were recovered by splitting into halves.

Not downloaded: the yearly bulk files for 2020 to 2025 (170 to 225 MB each, above the cap); tile, mda, meso and structure bulk files; shapefile attribute tables beyond the member list; KML and GeoJSON attributes beyond counts; nx3meso, nx3tvs, nx3mda and nx3structure contents (only the period of record was checked).
NWS technical attachment ta9827 (WebFetch) was an image-based PDF that could not be read. Not used. The ICD was read from the NWS copy found by search (not the NCEI-linked path, which is 404).

Radar site coordinates come from the IEM network list (secondary). Beam height and radar-geometry tests were not computed: they need VCP elevation angles, antenna heights and terrain (W5). W1's -999 question stays open.
The nx3hail:inv inventory LAST_UPDATED time zone is not stated; lag values are good to about 0.2 day.
Two products requested in the brief are unavailable: plsr is not a SWDI dataset and warn is not accepted by the live service (HTTP 500). Warning history must come from W3.
The distinct storm-day keys (WSR_ID, CELL_ID, UTC day) are approximate; no clustering rule into events is proposed here.
open_questions: What do PROB, SEVPROB and MAXSIZE -999 mean in nx3hail_all? 99.2% of the Montana -999 rows lie beyond 124 nmi (an inference); the documents do not define them. NCEI should confirm.
Why are there no nx3hail or nx3hail_all records from 2025-06-15 12:00 to 24:00 UTC, while the inventory reports 24 coverage hours and 143 files? Is the archive still incomplete for that day?
Why are there no records for 2026-10-13? Outage, processing gap or no detections?
Will NCEI regenerate the February 2026 bulk file? What is the stability of files labelled 'experimental'?
Do the exact duplicate rows (for example 278 on 2023-05-24) reflect a known archive issue? Should the duplicates be removed by the consumer?
Is the one-year row limit documented in the usage text intended to be enforced? The observed limit is 744 hours for row output and grouped counts.

Is there a newer NWS HI product definition after RPG Build 18.0 (2018)? Check the ROC build information file list before any product wording relies on it (ROC index 403 and guessed build pages 404 in review).
What are the VCP lowest elevation angles and antenna heights for KTFX, KBLX, KGGW and KMSX? Needed with terrain (W5) for the W1 -999 radar-geometry test.
An NWS-primary source for the Montana radar coordinates (the IEM list was used here).
The SPC 1.75 inch report near Benchland (2025-06-15): time, location and whether SWDI or MRMS support it (W2 for SPC; W1 for MRMS units).
Whether NCEI's public domain statement covers derived counts and the bulk 'experimental' files, and what attribution NCEI asks for. Left to the legal review (W10).
Event clustering rule for repeated detections of one storm (WSR_ID, CELL_ID, time gaps). Not proposed here.
Why are there no records or inventory rows for 2025-01-12 to 2025-01-19?
Do the 2023-05-24 duplicates (all from radar KGGW) reflect a known KGGW issue?
Does the archive omit 0% probability cells, which the ICD allows?

programs.name: NCEI Severe Weather Data Inventory web services
programs.what_it_gives: Point records of NEXRAD Level-III hail signatures (nx3hail filtered; nx3hail_all unfiltered) and of tornado vortex, mesocyclone and storm-structure signatures, plus lightning (nldn, restricted). Date ranges up to 744 hours per row request; bounding box or 0.1-degree tile; csv, json, xml, geojson, shp and kmz. Period of record 1992-05-07 to 2026-10-14 for the NEXRAD datasets.
programs.cost_or_licence: No charge or licence fee stated on the pages read. NOAA environmental data 'are in the public domain in the United States' (NCEI-PD-10-2-02 section 4a). Service note on the product page: 'Current Impact: Intermittent degraded order fulfillment services.'

programs.name: NCEI SWDI bulk CSV (database-csv/v2)
programs.what_it_gives: Yearly gzip CSV files for hail (1995 to 2025), monthly files for 2026, plus tile-day and mesocyclone files. Yearly hail files are 170.5 to 225.0 MB gzipped for 2020 to 2025 (1.16 GB together). Headers carry 'This file contains experimental data.'
programs.cost_or_licence: HTTP download; no fee stated; labelled experimental. The February 2026 monthly file is incomplete (10 of 28 days).
